research_mode: official Home Office, ONS and GOV.UK primary methodology only; each claim has a fail-closed limitation; no parcel result, exact incident location, local risk score, candidate value or business result claimed

sources.name: Official-statistics-in-development status
verified_claims: Police misconduct statistics are designated Official Statistics in Development while the series and data collection continue to develop.
limitations: The developing designation requires caution and does not support precise force rankings without quality context.

sources.name: Territorial-force finalised-case scope
verified_claims: The annual release covers cases finalised by the 43 territorial police forces in England and Wales during the financial year.
limitations: It does not cover every police body, open case or matter outside the defined finalised-case scope.

sources.name: Misconduct-threshold focus
verified_claims: The release primarily focuses on allegations meeting thresholds for misconduct, gross misconduct or criminal investigation, including conduct and recordable conduct matters and complaints investigated under Special Procedures.
limitations: The published scope is not a count of every complaint or concern raised about policing.

sources.name: Centurion data source
verified_claims: The statistics are derived from Centurion, the operational professional-standards recording system used by territorial forces.
limitations: Administrative-system data reflect recording practice and are not independently observed events.

sources.name: 2020-regulations coverage
verified_claims: From year ending March 2022 the statistics cover cases handled under the 2020 regulations, creating an undercount while older-regulation cases remain outside the collection.
limitations: Totals must not be interpreted as all misconduct cases finalised in the year.

sources.name: Pre-February-2020 case exclusion
verified_claims: Cases that came to force attention before 1 February 2020 are not included in the later-series scope.
limitations: A missing historical case cannot be inferred to have been absent or dismissed.

sources.name: Local-system omission
verified_claims: Forces may record some cases on local systems rather than Centurion, particularly some staff conduct matters and complaints outside Schedule 3.
limitations: Centurion-based totals are likely to undercount all cases and cannot be treated as complete force inventories.

sources.name: Finalised-case extraction
verified_claims: Because Centurion is a live operational system, the collection focuses on cases finalised during the financial year.
limitations: Finalised-case statistics do not show the full stock of ongoing cases or current risk.

sources.name: Year-ending-2021 investigating filter
verified_claims: The first release used an 'investigating' status filter that could omit cases incorrectly coded or include cases incorrectly marked.
limitations: The first-year extraction is not directly comparable without recognising the filter risk.

sources.name: Removal of investigating filter
verified_claims: From year ending March 2022 the investigating-status filter was removed and all finalised cases were supplied.
limitations: Direct comparison between year ending March 2021 and later releases is not valid on a like-for-like basis.

sources.name: Outside-Schedule-3 undercount
verified_claims: Complaints handled outside Schedule 3 may be stored on local systems and are likely undercounted, so the bulletin focuses on Schedule 3 allegations.
limitations: Published complaint totals must not be represented as every complaint received by a force.

sources.name: Subject-reference double-counting risk
verified_claims: In year ending March 2022 a person involved in separate cases could receive different subject references and be counted multiple times.
limitations: The case-level subject count must not be treated as a unique-person count for that year.

sources.name: Staff-reference methodology change
verified_claims: From year ending March 2023 the Home Office used a stable staff reference to count a person once across cases.
limitations: The methodology change creates a comparability break with previous individual counts.

sources.name: Gender-field interpretation
verified_claims: The Centurion gender field may contain a mixture of gender and sex data, although statistics report the categories as collected.
limitations: The categories must not be treated as a harmonised measure of either sex or gender identity.

sources.name: Suspension-source differences
verified_claims: Misconduct suspension data come from Centurion while police-workforce suspension data come from force HR systems and use different inclusion rules.
limitations: Counts from the two publications must not be combined or directly compared without reconciling definitions.

sources.name: Live-system extraction-date difference
verified_claims: Misconduct and workforce extracts can differ because they come from live systems on different dates.
limitations: A discrepancy between releases is not by itself proof of error or misconduct under-recording.

sources.name: Reopened-case counting risk
verified_claims: Appeals or later criminal proceedings can cause Centurion cases to be reopened, creating possible double counting between years or undercounting later outcomes.
limitations: Financial-year case counts may change with reopening practice and should not be treated as immutable case histories.

sources.name: Force validation before publication
verified_claims: Home Office quality assurance flags issues to forces and sends data back before publication for confirmation and correction where possible.
limitations: Validation reduces but does not eliminate administrative-data error.

sources.name: Misconduct QA checks
verified_claims: Quality checks include missing or incomplete data, inconsistencies, extreme values and large unexplained year-on-year changes.
limitations: Passing automated or manual QA does not prove every record is complete or correctly classified.

sources.name: Continuing methodology development
verified_claims: The Home Office states that misconduct statistics and their QA processes will continue to develop, including future trend analysis once comparable data are available.
limitations: Current series limitations must remain visible and no unsupported long-term trend should be inferred.
